name: pinned-steps
title: Pinned steps
author: Eduardo Retana
description: A sticky visual column that cross-fades as each step crosses the center of the viewport. Narrow viewports and reduced motion stack the step with its visual.

meta.descriptionEs: La columna visual se queda fija y cambia con el paso que cruza el centro. En estrecho, o con movimiento reducido, cada paso lleva su visual.

examples.title: Pasos fijos
examples.description: La columna visual se queda mientras los pasos avanzan.

examples.title: Glosario
examples.description: Los diez términos de scroll, con demos propias.

meta.usage: <PinnedSteps label="Firing" steps={[{ id: "dry", title: "Drying", body: "The door stays ajar.", visual }]} />

api.name: steps
api.description: id, title, body, and visual. decorative hides the visual from assistive tech. A visual with data is a polite live region while it is the active one.

api.name: minWidth
api.description: Stack below this viewport width. Default 768. Shared with use-min-width.

api.name: label / emptyLabel
api.description: Accessible name of the step region, and the copy for an empty list.

api.name: className / visualClassName / stepClassName
api.description: Root, sticky visual column, and each step. Defaults are a two-column pin and an 80vh step.

docs: Clean-room scrollytelling. No Motion UI or Motion+ source. On a wide screen with motion allowed, the visual column is position sticky and each step is in normal flow. One IntersectionObserver per step uses rootMargin -50% 0px -50% 0px, so the step that crosses the center is active. The cross-fade is opacity and transform only, timed with motionPresets. Below 768px, and when motion-preference says reduce, each step stacks with its visual and nothing sticks. A decorative visual is aria-hidden. A visual that carries data uses aria-live polite while it is showing. Answer no if the CLI asks to overwrite use-min-width, motion-preference, or another file the host already has. The item ships no theme, cssVars, or fixed colors.
